steps.title: Design top and bottom molds
steps.instruction: Create SolidWorks part files for the top and bottom channels, define reference planes, sketch and extrude the substrate box, add 2‑D and 3‑D features, save each part, then assemble them to verify fit and create an assembly containing multiple copies for the master mold.

substeps.instruction: Create a dedicated folder for all SolidWorks documents and never rename files directly; use Save As with the option to move all references.
Create the top channel part (e.g., “Final Top.SLDPRT”) and add X, Y, Z reference planes offset 0 mm from the Top, Right and Front planes.
Create a sketch on the Front plane, draw a rectangle anchored at the intersection of the three reference planes, and boss‑extrude it to form the substrate box.
On the Z reference plane, sketch all 2‑D features (entry/exit holes, rectangular channels) at a single depth and perform an extruded cut.
Create additional reference planes offset from X or Y to generate 3‑D features such as curved channels, then extrude cut them.
Save the completed top part, then Save As a new file (e.g., “Final Base.SLDPRT”) to serve as the bottom channel; edit as needed, adding guide‑marker circles for alignment.
Create an assembly file containing the top and bottom parts, mate them to verify geometry, but do not define reference geometry in the assembly.
Create a second assembly that imports multiple copies of the top and bottom parts, aligns them into a contiguous block, and export this assembly for Fusion tool‑path generation.

steps.title: Generate Fusion toolpaths
steps.instruction: In Autodesk Fusion, define the stock, create tool libraries for the 500 µm square and 200 µm ball‑nose end mills, input their dimensions and flutes, set RPM, disable coolant, enter calculated feed rates (chip load 4 %), and program the cutting sequence using clearing, boring, rough pocketing, low‑stepover finishing, and marker‑hole steps.

substeps.instruction: Create or select a tool library; add two tools: 500 µm square 2‑flute (diameter 0.5 mm, spindle speed 10 000 rpm, feed 1.005 in/min, stepdown 0.25 mm, stepover 0.125 mm) and 200 µm ball 2‑flute (diameter 0.2 mm, spindle speed 30 000 rpm, feed 0.483 in/min, stepdown 0.1 mm, stepover 0.05 mm).
Set coolant to Disabled and ensure the 500 µm tool is indexed first, the 200 µm tool second.
Define the stock dimensions matching the acrylic sheet and set the origin at the lower‑left corner of the top face.
Program the following cuts (using the parameters in Table 4):
• 500 µm tool – 2D pocket on bottom channel with one 0.1 mm stepdown.
• 500 µm tool – bore all 0.5 mm entry/exit holes.
• 200 µm tool – 2D pocket on top channel (rough material removal).
• 200 µm tool – low‑stepover parallel facing on top channel (max stepdown 0.02 mm).
• 200 µm tool – 2D circular cuts for 0.5 mm alignment holes.
Save the generated G‑code (.tap) to a USB drive.

steps.title: Prepare and run micro‑mill
steps.instruction: Cut acrylic stock, mount it, home and probe the CNC, install the first end mill, set work coordinates, run the G‑code, perform tool changes as prompted, then clean and shut down the machine.

substeps.instruction: Cut an acrylic block at least 5 mm larger than the design in each dimension (≥5 mm × 5 mm × 5 mm extra stock).
Turn on the machine control box, spindle control box, and computer; wait ≥2 min for Mach3 to start without bugs.
Attach double‑sided tape to the bottom of the stock and secure it to the chuck; verify the stock orientation (long side = +X).
Open Mach3, press Reset, raise the spindle to a safe height, and install the first end mill securely.
Start the camera view and aim the air‑hose at the tool tip for chip removal.
Click Home → Probe to calibrate the tool tip.
Jog the tool to the bottom‑left corner of the stock (the Fusion origin) without touching the surface; leave a small margin of stock around the origin.
Lower slowly in Z using step‑jog (1–0.1 µm); listen for the spindle‑contact sound and confirm with the camera.
When the tip contacts the surface, turn off the spindle, then click Work Coordinates → Zero All to set the work origin.
Copy the G‑code file from the USB drive to the computer desktop, load it in Mach3, start the spindle manually, then click Cycle Start twice.
During tool changes, wait for spindle stop, replace the tool, probe again, and click Cycle Start; never Home or Home + Probe during a cut.
After the program finishes, verify the spindle is off, remove the part, vacuum the work area, then turn off air, software, machine, and computer.

steps.title: Cast positive PDMS master molds
steps.instruction: Line the acrylic top and bottom molds with tape, mix PDMS and crosslinker 5:1, degas, cure at 65 °C for 2 h, then bake the PDMS cast at 120 °C overnight.

substeps.instruction: Place each acrylic mold in a container or line its perimeter with tape to contain PDMS.
Weigh PDMS and curing agent in a 5:1 ratio (by mass) into a plastic container.
Mix at 2 200 rpm for 3 min in an orbital mixer (or stir manually ≥5 min).
Tare a gram scale with the acrylic mold, then pour PDMS until the layer is ~0.5 cm thick; record the poured mass for future casts.
Place the mold in a vacuum desiccator for 30 min; if bubbles persist, blow them with compressed air or a Pasteur pipette and repeat until clear.
Cure in a 65 °C oven for 2 h.
Demold the PDMS, then place the PDMS master in a 120 °C oven overnight (~16 h).
Note: Do not bake the acrylic negative at 120 °C; only the PDMS cast receives the overnight bake.

steps.title: Cast microfluidic PDMS devices
steps.instruction: Using the PDMS‑positive master molds, mix PDMS/crosslinker 10:1, degas, cure at 65 °C, then peel and cut individual channels.

substeps.instruction: Line a larger container or tape the edges of each PDMS‑positive master as in Figure 7B.
Weigh PDMS and crosslinker in a 10:1 mass‑to‑mass ratio, mix at 2 200 rpm for 3 min.
Tare a gram scale with the master, pour PDMS to achieve ~0.5 cm thickness; note the mass for reproducibility.
Degas in a vacuum desiccator for 30 min.
Cure flat in a 65 °C oven for 2 h (do not over‑bake).
Allow to cool to room temperature, then use a straight‑edge razor or sturdy scalpel to outline the PDMS slab and peel it off the master carefully.
Cut the slab into individual channel pieces and store each on masking tape to keep surfaces clean (usable ≤6 months).

steps.title: Functionalize porous membranes
steps.instruction: Perform plasma oxidation of polycarbonate membranes, then silanize with APTES at 80 °C for 20 min, followed by overnight drying.

substeps.instruction: In a fume hood, place a 400 mL glass beaker with 190 mL ultrapure water and a magnetic stir bar; set stirring to ~4/10 (no heat yet).
Draw 10 mL APTES from its stock (do not remove the septum) with a 16 G needle and syringe; add slowly to the water over ~20 s while stirring.
Cover the beaker with aluminum foil, set a hotplate to 350 °C, and heat until the solution reaches 80 °C (monitor with a laser thermometer; actual hotplate temperature may differ).
While heating, plasma‑oxidize membranes in batches of four (50 W, 1 min) on both sides; cut each membrane two‑thirds around its holder with scalpel/forceps, keeping it attached to the holder.
After all 12 membranes are oxidized twice, remove the foil, and place the membranes one‑by‑one into the 80 °C APTES solution; start a 20 min timer and keep temperature at 80 ± 5 °C.
After 20 min, turn off the hotplate, keep stirring, and let the solution cool for another 20 min.
Using heat‑protected gloves, remove the beaker, then fish each membrane out with forceps onto a paper towel; avoid contact with any surface.
Dispose of APTES‑contaminated waste according to hazardous‑waste protocols; rinse the beaker several times with water (water waste to chemical waste) before normal sink disposal.
Dry membranes in the closed fume hood overnight (≥16 h). Store dried membranes (still in holders) in a cool, dry, dust‑free place for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Assemble sandwich device
steps.instruction: Punch inlet/outlet holes, align top and bottom PDMS channels with functionalized membranes, plasma‑bond layers, and bake to finalize the device.

substeps.instruction: Cut functionalized membranes into rectangles large enough to fully cover each channel.
Using 1.5 mm biopsy punches, create entrance and exit holes only on the top channel.
Remove top and bottom PDMS channels from masking tape, align them using the guide markers, and trim corners vertically for easier alignment.
Place 1–3 top channels (channel side up) with their membranes on a flat surface covered with lab tape; pin membrane edges with a small piece of tape.
Plasma‑oxidize the top channel plus membrane (50 W, 30 s).
Within 30 s, lift the membrane from the tape and lay it onto the top channel; ensure immediate contact to avoid wrinkling.
Plasma‑oxidize both top and bottom layers (channel side up) again (50 W, 30 s).
Immediately align the top channel (with membrane) onto the bottom channel, press gently for ~5 s to promote bonding.
Place the assembled device in a 65 °C oven for 20–30 min to solidify the bond (do not exceed temperature or time to avoid brittleness or membrane wrinkling).

steps.title: Prepare pipette tip reservoirs
steps.instruction: Cut P1000 and P200 pipette tips to create cutoff reservoirs for media loading and store them sterile.

substeps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, cut a P1000 tip about halfway down; repeat to obtain four cutoff tips per device.
Cut a P200 tip with a sterile filter just below the filter; store all cut tips under sterile conditions indefinitely.

steps.title: Prepare collagen coating solution
steps.instruction: Make 91 µg/mL rat‑tail collagen‑I in PBS at pH 9 on ice, filter‑sterilize, and keep at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add collagen stock to PBS on ice to achieve 91 µg/mL (≈26 µL collagen per mL PBS; adjust per lot‑specific concentration).
Adjust pH to 9 with 1 M NaOH.
Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter and store at 4 °C (stable ≤1 month).

steps.title: Sterilize and coat devices
steps.instruction: Clean devices with ethanol, rinse with PBS, fill top channels with collagen solution, and incubate for 90 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: Place devices in a sterile Petri dish; wipe outer surfaces with scotch tape.
Add 70 % ethanol to both top and bottom channels, let sit 30 s, then aspirate.
Rinse channels with 3 mL PBS each, aspirate leaving channels air‑filled.
Pipette ~13 µL collagen solution into each top channel (surface tension prevents bleed‑through).
Incubate devices for 90 min in a 37 °C, 95 % humidity, 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Prepare airway epithelial cells
steps.instruction: Passage SAEC cells to ~60‑80 % confluence, resuspend in SAGM medium at 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL.

substeps.instruction: Follow Lonza’s instructions for passaging SAEC (catalog CC‑2547).
Count cells and adjust concentration to 3 × 10⁶ cells/mL in SAGM™ Small Airway Epithelial Cell Growth Medium.

steps.title: Seed cells into microfluidic channels
steps.instruction: Load media reservoirs, replace collagen with media, add cells to the top channel, and perform gentle aspiration to position cells.

substeps.instruction: Insert the cutoff P1000 tips into each channel inlet (except the T‑channel, which remains plugged).
Add 200 µL SAGM medium to the bottom channel via the cutoff tip reservoir.
After the 90‑min collagen incubation, dispense 100 µL medium into the top channel, then aspirate the collagen‑medium mixture leaving a thin film covering the channel.
Add 50 µL of the cell suspension (3 × 10⁶ cells/mL) into the top channel reservoir farthest from the T‑junction.
Aspirate 20–30 µL from the opposite top reservoir to gently draw cells into the channel.
Incubate for 2 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to allow attachment.

steps.title: Remove unattached cells and equilibrate media
steps.instruction: Perform three gentle wash cycles in the top channel and equalize media heights in all reservoirs.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL medium to the inlet reservoir, wait 30 s, then remove 100 µL from the outlet; repeat twice more.
Inspect for cell aggregates and remove if present.
Fill all four tip reservoirs (top inlet, top outlet, bottom inlet, bottom outlet) until the liquid height is ~1 inch in each, ensuring equal hydrostatic pressure across the membrane.

steps.title: Maintain devices in culture
steps.instruction: Place devices on a rocker plate to generate bidirectional flow and change media daily for up to two weeks.

substeps.instruction: Put the Petri dish with devices on a rocker so the fluid sloshes from one reservoir to the other and back.
Every 24 h, completely replace the medium in both top and bottom channels.
Continue daily changes for the duration of the experiment (up to 14 days).

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: Viola et al. [8]. Liquid plug propagation in computer-controlled microfluidic airway-on-a-chip with semi-circular microchannels. Lab Chip .
